text: wallpaper-engine-dsh 是面向 DSH 网页端的壁纸背景插件。它接入网页主机的 HTTP 服务，并在浏览器界面加入专属设置区，把本机 Wallpaper Engine 库中的视频和网页壁纸呈现在聊天界面后方。用户可以浏览和搜索壁纸、调整画面适配与取景、设置模糊和玻璃效果、管理轮播列表，还能查看帧率并设置隐藏标签页或低电量时暂停。适合希望用本地动态壁纸个性化 DSH 网页界面的用户；需要安装 Wallpaper Engine 并使用 DSH web，不需要额外 API 密钥。

wallpaper-engine-dsh adds local Wallpaper Engine backgrounds to DSH web. Browse and search video or web wallpapers, adjust their framing and visual effects, create rotation lists, and monitor playback from a settings section. It requires Wallpaper Engine and DSH web, with no API key.
想把自己的动态壁纸放到 DSH 网页聊天背景里。
有没有办法从本机壁纸库挑一张当网页背景？
我想搜索本地壁纸，并在会话界面后面播放视频壁纸。
让 DSH 网页能轮流切换我收藏的几张壁纸。
能不能裁切、缩放和移动背景画面，让它适合屏幕？
页面切到后台或电池电量低时暂停壁纸播放。
Can I use my local Wallpaper Engine library as the background for DSH in a browser?
I want to search and play a video or web wallpaper behind my chat window.
wallpaper-engine-dsh 的功能「浏览本地壁纸」：扫描 Wallpaper Engine 项目并列出浏览器可播放的视频和网页壁纸。打开设置区即可搜索并选择壁纸。
wallpaper-engine-dsh 的功能「壁纸轮播」：创建包含多张壁纸的列表并设定顺序或随机播放。开启 Auto-rotate 后，列表至少有两张可用壁纸时会自动切换。
wallpaper-engine-dsh 的功能「画面取景」：用户可选择适配方式，再进入 Adjust 模式拖动画面、缩放和旋转壁纸；选项保存在浏览器设置中。
wallpaper-engine-dsh 的功能「播放状态监测」：设置区显示当前帧率，并可配置标签页隐藏或设备低电量时自动暂停壁纸。
wallpaper-engine-dsh 的使用提示：壁纸选择和各项效果设置保存在浏览器 localStorage 中；更换浏览器存储后不会自动同步。（见 lib/client.js:354）

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · wallpaper-engine-dsh：A DSH bundle that turns your local **Wallpaper Engine** library into the live background of the DSH web GUI (`dsh web`). Video wallpapers play behind the chat, web wallpapers render in place, and everything in between — crossfade transitions, liquid-glass panels, a legibility veil that adapts to any wallpaper, manual framing, rotation lists, search, and a bilingual UI — is controlled from its own dedicated settings section.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Features：**The library, rendered live.** The grid lists every wallpaper the browser can genuinely render — video and web wallpapers. Scene and application wallpapers are Wallpaper Engine's private `.pkg` scene packages; since no browser can execute them, they are filtered out rather than offered as degraded stills. Everything listed plays for real, badged Video or Web, and a search box narrows large libraries by title or workshop id instantly.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Features：**Legibility on any wallpaper.** Text stays readable by construction, not by luck. The material is permanently dark — one glass recipe, whatever the shell or OS light/dark setting says — and the veil is always black, so a pitch-black wallpaper can never swallow the UI (pair the shell with its dark theme, which the dark material assumes). On top of that, a Smart veil samples the wallpaper's brightness every few seconds and automatically strengthens the veil when a scene drifts too bright for the light-on-dark text (web wallpapers' pixels are unreadable inside the sandbox, so their preview still stands in as the sample). While a wallpaper is active, dropdown menus, the slash-command popup, the queue-dock panel, the settings dialog, and the image lightbox all render as frosted glass: the shell's own menu primitive carries an isolation property that silently kills its internal blur layer, so the plugin applies the blur on the surface element itself and deepens the menu fill, keeping overlay text readable over any wallpaper. The glass material itself follows Apple's Liquid Glass cues: an asymmetric edge specular (the top bevel catches more light th

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Features：**Manual framing.** Pick a base layout — Cover, Contain, Stretch, Original, or Free — then frame the shot yourself. **Adjust** opens the live wallpaper fullscreen: scroll to zoom, drag to pan. In the seamless layouts the picture already fills the screen at 100% — zoom in with the wheel first and panning unlocks (the hint bar says so). In the first four layouts the crop is clamped so the image always fills the screen with no exposed edges; **Free** places the wallpaper at natural size on a black canvas where it can be dragged anywhere, zoomed from 0.1× to 4×, and rotated to any angle (±90° buttons or Alt+drag), with just enough kept on screen that it can never be dragged out of sight. **Mirror** flips the wallpaper horizontally and works in every layout — a flip never exposes an edge. Esc or Done finishes, the framing persists, and **Reset crop** restores the default in one click. Web wallpapers take the same select and the same zoom/pan/rotate framing — the transform applies to the iframe directly.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Features：**Four live sliders.** Wallpaper blur, Scrim, Borders, and Glass — every change lands instantly and persists. Blur renders in place: composition, layout, and crop stay identical at every blur level, and within one blur radius of the screen edge the picture fades softly into the veil beneath the UI chrome. A whisper of dither noise keeps smooth gradients band-free; at zero blur the media bypasses the filter pipeline entirely for bit-exact pixels. The Glass slider's colour melt is anchored to the shell's own menu material: at the 40px ceiling it reproduces the host recipe blur(40px) saturate(150%) exactly, so full glass reads as one system with the shell's native frost. Below that it steers the melt from liquid (the ~8–12px zone — the default is 8px, the clearest band) toward frosted; the vibrancy stays at the host's saturate(150%) throughout. The same slider scales the edge-specular strength (thicker glass catches more light) and gates the refraction lens; at zero the whole glass filter chain collapses to none and the surfaces fall back to their translucent fills. The Borders slider drives the glass's own hairline rim: the 0.35 default is a hos

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Features：**Rotation lists.** Build any number of carousel lists, each with its own wallpapers, interval (1–120 min), and order (sequence or random). Auto-rotate arms once the active list holds at least two usable wallpapers; the status row always reports whether rotation is actually running. Your first playable Wallpaper Engine playlist is imported automatically on first run; any other playlist can be imported into any list.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Features：**Resource monitor.** A live FPS readout with a low-framerate hint, plus optional auto-pause when the tab is hidden or the battery runs low. `prefers-reduced-motion` starts videos paused.

**Bilingual.** The UI follows the shell's Language setting (Chinese/English) with a manual override in the picker.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Features：**Resilient playback.** Switches and clears crossfade smoothly. Media that repeatedly fails to decode retries once with fresh tokens, then falls back to the preview still with a note in the status row; an entry with nothing to fall back on is cleared rather than left on a dead layer — and the next Refresh retries the live media. Refresh re-issues every URL and swaps it into the live element in place, so playback position survives. Background inventory rebuilds reuse the same URLs and never touch a playing stream.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add wallpaper-engine-dsh
```

Or from a checkout (live-linked for development):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Weilv-D/wallpaper-engine-dsh.git
dsh plugin --profile web add link:<absolute path to the cloned folder>
```

Restart `dsh web`, open **Settings** from the sidebar, and pick **Wallpaper**.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Usage：1. Pick a wallpaper from the thumbnail grid — it fades in behind the app. Use the search box to narrow large libraries.
2. **Pause/Play** controls video playback; **Close** fades the wallpaper out; **Refresh** rescans the library — new workshop subscriptions appear without reloading the page, and any demoted wallpaper retries its live media.
3. Tune the blend with the sliders. On busy wallpapers, raise **Scrim** and **Borders** until text is comfortable; Smart veil handles it automatically when enabled. The UI follows DSH's light/dark theme on its own.
4. Use the **Fit** row for the base layout, then **Adjust** to pan and zoom the crop directly on the canvas.
5. Create rotation lists with **New**, fill them from the grid or import a WE playlist, then enable **Auto-rotate**.
6. The resource row shows the current frame rate and the two auto-pause switches.
wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Usage：Your selection and every knob persist in the browser's `localStorage`.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Desktop：The desktop shell and the browser share the same frontend and the same injection pipeline; the `platform: "web"` declaration works as-is, with no separate desktop package.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Desktop：- **Windows**: the main window is opaque and the wallpaper renders at the DOM layer. The window-controls strip at the top is an opaque host-owned overlay; the plugin blends the wallpaper into it with a short fade in the overlay's own colour, and the fade switches off in fullscreen.
- **macOS**: the shell sidebar is the system's native vibrant material, so what shows behind the wallpaper there is the system material rather than the wallpaper itself — host behaviour.
- **With system transparency effects off** (`prefers-reduced-transparency`), all glass and blur falls back to solid surfaces; the wallpaper stays, and legibility is carried by the veil and the solids. With **increase contrast** on (`prefers-contrast: more`), the glass fills go near-opaque and the hairline ring steps up to a solid border, while the blur itself stays.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · How it works：- A **host plugin** discovers the Wallpaper Engine install (Steam registry entry, `libraryfolders.vdf`, standard probe paths across Windows/macOS/Linux), enumerates projects from the default/my-projects folders and the workshop, keeps only the browser-renderable kinds, and serves a JSON inventory plus the media bytes over same-origin routes:
  - `GET /we-background/inventory[?refresh=1]`
  - `GET /we-background/media/<token>[/<entry file or asset>…]` — with HTTP Range support for video seeking. Web wallpapers are addressed at their entry file (e.g. `…/media/<token>/index.html`), so the document URL mirrors the project directory and the wallpaper's own relative references (scripts, styles, images, fetches) resolve exactly where Wallpaper Engine would resolve them. Media responses carry `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` so wallpapers inside the sandboxed iframe (an opaque origin) can still `fetch()` their own assets.
  - `GET /we-background/preview/<token>`
- A **browser plugin** renders the chosen wallpaper on a fixed layer behind the app frame, contributes the settings UI, and keeps every effect on DSH design tokens so themes apply cleanly.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · How it works：Media serving is defensive by design: tokens are unguessable 72-bit values, stable across inventory rebuilds (an in-flight stream is never killed by a background refresh) and re-minted only on an explicit refresh; sub-asset paths are contained lexically and re-verified against the real filesystem so symlinks cannot escape their wallpaper directory; HTML and SVG responses carry a `sandbox` CSP so they can never execute against the DSH origin; the wallpaper iframe additionally pins a neutral `color-scheme`, so the shell's dark-theme scheme never leaks into — and breaks — third-party wallpaper apps; the wildcard CORS on media only lets a caller who already knows a token read bytes it could already request — the token stays the capability, and the server is loopback-only; and responses that would come up short destroy themselves rather than truncate silently. The host answers from a 30-second inventory cache, resolves discovery asynchronously off the request path, and caches it for ten minutes. The bundle registers no model tools and adds no prompt text.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Limitations：- Scene and application wallpapers are not listed: they are Wallpaper Engine's private `.pkg` scene packages, and their live animation can only be rendered by Wallpaper Engine itself on the desktop.
- Web wallpapers run isolated from the page's storage, so ones that persist state across loads won't keep it.
- Web wallpapers with sound may stay silent until you interact with the page — browsers gate audio in sandboxed documents on a user gesture, and wallpapers that rely on Wallpaper Engine's system-audio feed (visualizers) have no signal to draw from.
- Video codecs are bounded by what the browser can decode. H.264/AVC, VP8/VP9, and AV1 play natively; workshop videos compressed with H.265/HEVC cannot be software-decoded on most machines — previously a solid black screen, now detected as "playing but zero decoded frames" and automatically demoted to the preview still with a status note. Transcoding to H.264 mp4 or VP9 webm restores full playback.
- The glass effect reads DSH design tokens; if a future shell redesign renames them, frosting degrades to plain transparency.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Development：```sh
npm install        # builds lib/client.js via the prepare hook
npm test           # unit tests for the pure core + wire-level host integration
npm run build      # regenerate lib/client.js from src/client.js
npm run verify     # boot the emitted bundle in a vm sandbox and assert behaviour

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Development：Layout: `lib/core.js` (pure, tested logic), `lib/index.js` (host plugin), `src/client.js` (browser source) → `lib/client.js` (built artifact; do not hand-edit). `npm run prepublishOnly` runs the full gate: test → build → verify.

wallpaper-engine-dsh README · Releasing：Releases publish automatically via GitHub Actions and npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC, no stored tokens). One command does everything locally:

```sh
npm run release          # patch bump; also release:minor / release:major
```

It bumps `version`, commits, tags `v<version>`, and pushes both. The tag push triggers the publish workflow: full gate → tag ↔ version check → `npm publish --provenance` → the GitHub Release is created automatically with generated notes.
